1 2 3 ### High-performance audio engine for React Native based on web audio api specification 4 5 [![NPM latest](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/react-native-audio-api/latest)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-audio-api) 6 [![NPM nightly](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/react-native-audio-api/audio-api-nightly)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-audio-api?activeTab=versions) 7
8 [![github ci](https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-audio-api/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-audio-api/actions/workflows/ci.yml) 9 [![Audio Api tests](https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-audio-api/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-audio-api/actions/workflows/tests.yml) 10 11 `react-native-audio-api` provides system for controlling audio in React Native environment compatible with Web Audio API specification, 12 allowing developers to generate and modify audio in exact same way it is possible in browsers. 13 14 ## Installation 15 16 check out the [Getting Started](https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-audio-api/docs/fundamentals/getting-started) section of our documentation for detailed instructions! 17 18 ## Roadmap 19 20 ### Planned 21 22 ### 23 24 - **DynamicCompressorNode 〽️**
25 Reduce the volume of loud sounds and boost quieter nodes to balance the audio signal, avoid clipping or distorted sounds 26 27 - **Audio tag 🏷️**
28 Simple ability to play and buffer audio, with all of the most commonly used functions, same as on the web, without the need to create and manipulate an audio graph. 29 30 - **MIDI support 🎸**
31 Complementary lib for react-native-audio-api, that will allow to communicate with MIDI devices or read/write MIDI files. 32 33 - **Spatial Audio 🛢️**
34 manipulate audio in 3D space 35 36 - **Noise Cancellation 🦇**
37 System-based active noise and echo cancellation support 38 39 ### 40 41 - **Recording to file 📼**
42 Fully customizable recording to a file. Choose a file format, quality and other parameters. Fully integrated with the audio graph. 43 44 - **Playback and recording notification system 🔔**
45 Control playback and recording from the notification center / lock screen and create custom notification layouts. 46 47 - **Wave Shaper Node 🎸**
48 Create custom nonlinear distortion effects. No need to buy guitar pedals anymore! 49 50 - **IIR Filter Node 🧪**
51 Implement custom digital filters using feedforward and feedback coefficients. 52 53 ### 54 55 - **Decoding and utility modules 🔧**
56 Decode and modify audio data without the need to create AudioContext first through a set of utility classes 57 58 - **Convolver Node 🐐**
59 Realistic reverb and spatial effects in the browser by applying impulse responses. It makes audio sound like it’s being played in real spaces, from small rooms to cathedrals, or through hardware like amps and speakers 60 61 - **JS Audio Worklets V2 🐎**
62 Customize the process pipeline with JS functions running on audio thread. 63 64 ### 65 66 - **JS Audio Worklets V1 🐎**
67 Receive events and data callbacks from audio thread to synchronize with UI on UI thread. 68 69 ### 70 71 - **Decoding support for m4a/mp4/aac/ogg/opus 📁**
72 Decode m4a/mp4/aac/ogg/opus audio files, allowing for playback of these formats in the audio graph. 73 74 - **HLS streaming support** 🌊
75 Stream audio from HLS sources, allowing for playback of live audio streams or pre-recorded audio files. 76 77 ### 78 79 - **Microphone support 🎙️**
80 Grab audio data from device microphone or connected device, connect it to the audio graph or stream through the internet. 81 82 - **Custom Audio Processor ⚙️**

You can use it for audio playback, including standard pause and resume functionalities. 17 18 An `AudioBufferSourceNode` can be started only once, so if you want to play the same sound again you have to create a new one. 19 However, this node is very inexpensive to create, and what is crucial you can reuse same [`AudioBuffer`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer). 20 21

27 28 #### [`AudioNode`](/docs/core/audio-node#properties) properties 29 30 31 32 ## Constructor 33 34 [`BaseAudioContext.createBufferSource(options: AudioBufferBaseSourceNodeOptions)`](/docs/core/base-audio-context#createbuffersource) 35 36 ```jsx 37 interface AudioBufferBaseSourceNodeOptions { 38 pitchCorrection: boolean // specifies if pitch correction algorithm has to be available 39 } 40 ``` 41 42 :::caution 43 The pitch correction algorithm introduces processing latency. 44 As a result, when scheduling precise playback times, you should start input samples slightly ahead of the intended playback time. 45 For more details, see [getLatency()](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-base-source-node#getlatency). 46 47 If you plan to play multiple buffers one after another, consider using [AudioBufferQueueSourceNode](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-queue-source-node) 48 ::: 49 50 ## Example 51 52 ```tsx 53 import React, { useEffect, useRef, FC } from 'react'; 54 import { 55 AudioContext, 56 AudioBufferSourceNode, 57 } from 'react-native-audio-api'; 58 59 function App() { 60 const audioContextRef = useRef(null); 61 if (!audioContextRef.current) { 62 audioContextRef.current = new AudioContext(); 63 } 64 const audioBufferSource = audioContextRef.current.createBufferSource(); 65 const buffer = ...; // Load your audio buffer here 66 audioBufferSource.buffer = buffer; 67 audioBufferSource.connect(audioContextRef.current.destination); 68 audioBufferSource.start(audioContextRef.current.currentTime); 69 } 70 ``` 71 72 ## Properties 73 74 It inherits all properties from [`AudioBufferBaseSourceNode`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-base-source-node#properties). 75 76 | Name | Type | Description | 77 | :----: | :----: | :-------- | 78 | `buffer` | [`AudioBuffer`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer) | Associated `AudioBuffer`. | 79 | `loop` | `boolean` | Boolean indicating if audio data must be replayed after when end of the associated `AudioBuffer` is reached. | 80 | `loopSkip` | `boolean` | Boolean indicating if upon setting up `loopStart` we want to skip immediately to the loop start. | 81 | `loopStart` | `number` | Float value indicating the time, in seconds, at which playback of the audio must begin, if loop is true. | 82 | `loopEnd` | `number` | Float value indicating the time, in seconds, at which playback of the audio must end and loop back to `loopStart`, if loop is true. | 83 84 ## Methods 85 86 It inherits all methods from [`AudioBufferBaseSourceNode`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-base-source-node#methods). 87 88 ### `start` {#start} 89 90 Schedules the `AudioBufferSourceNode` to start playback of audio data contained in the associated [`AudioBuffer`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer), or starts to play immediately. 91 92 | Parameter | Type | Description | 93 | :---: | :---: | :---- | 94 | `when` | `number` | The time, in seconds, at which playback is scheduled to start. If `when` is less than [`AudioContext.currentTime`](/docs/core/base-audio-context#properties) or set to 0, the node starts playing immediately.
Default: `0`. | 95 | `offset` | `number` | The position, in seconds, within the audio buffer where playback begins.
The default value is `0`, which starts playback from the beginning of the buffer. If the offset exceeds the buffer’s [`duration`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer#properties) (or the defined [`loopEnd`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-source-node#properties) value), it’s automatically clamped to the valid range.
Offsets are calculated using the buffer’s natural sample rate rather than the current playback rate — so even if the sound is played at double speed, halfway through a 10-second buffer is still 5 seconds. | 96 | `duration` | `number` | The playback duration, in seconds. If not provided, playback continues until the sound ends naturally or is manually stopped with [`stop() method`](/docs/sources/audio-scheduled-source-node#stop).
Equivalent to calling `start(when, offset)` followed by `stop(when + duration)`. | 97 98 99 #### Errors: 100 101 | Error type | Description | 102 | :---: | :---- | 103 | `RangeError` | `when` is negative number. | 104 | `RangeError` | `offset` is negative number. | 105 | `RangeError` | `duration` is negative number. | 106 | `InvalidStateError` | If node has already been started once. | 107 108 #### Returns `undefined`. 109 110 111 ## Events 112 113 ### `onLoopEnded` 114 115 Sets (or remove) callback that will be fired when buffer source node reached the end of the loop and is looping back to `loopStart`. 116 You can remove callback either by passing `null` or calling `remove` on the returned subscription. 117 118 ```ts 119 const subscription = audioBufferSourceNode.onLoopEnded = () => { // setting the callback 120 console.log("loop ended"); 121 }; 122 123 subscription.remove(); // removal of the subscription 124 ``` 125 126 ## Remarks 127 128 #### `buffer` 129 - If is null, it outputs a single channel of silence (all samples are equal to 0). 130 131 #### `loop` 132 - Default value is false. 133 134 #### `loopStart` 135 - Default value is 0. 136 137 #### `loopEnd` 138 - Default value is `buffer.duration`. 139 140 #### `playbackRate` 141 - Default value is 1.0. 142 - Nominal range is -∞ to ∞. 143 - For example value of 1.0 plays audio at normal speed, whereas value of 2.0 plays audio twice as fast as normal speed. 144 - When created with `createBufferSource(true)` it is clamped to range 0 to 3 and uses pitch correction algorithm. 145 [result-id: r7]

1 --- 2 sidebar_position: 1 3 --- 4 5 import { Optional, ReadOnly, MobileOnly } from '@site/src/components/Badges'; 6 7 # BaseAudioContext 8 9 The `BaseAudioContext` interface acts as a supervisor of audio-processing graphs. It provides key processing parameters such as current time, output destination or sample rate. 10 Additionally, it is responsible for nodes creation and audio-processing graph's lifecycle management. 11 However, `BaseAudioContext` itself cannot be directly utilized, instead its functionalities must be accessed through one of its derived interfaces: [`AudioContext`](/docs/core/audio-context), [`OfflineAudioContext`](/docs/core/offline-audio-context). 12 13 #### Audio graph 14 15 An audio graph is a structured representation of audio processing elements and their connections within an audio context. 16 The graph consists of various types of nodes, each performing specific audio operations, connected in a network that defines the audio signal flow. 17 In general we can distinguish four types of nodes: 18 - Source nodes (e.g [`AudioBufferSourceNode`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-source-node), [`OscillatorNode`](/docs/sources/oscillator-node)) 19 - Effect nodes (e.g [`GainNode`](/docs/effects/gain-node), [`BiquadFilterNode`](/docs/effects/biquad-filter-node)) 20 - Analysis nodes (e.g [`AnalyserNode`](/docs/analysis/analyser-node)) 21 - Destination nodes (e.g [`AudioDestinationNode`](/docs/destinations/audio-destination-node)) 22 23 ![](/img/audio-graph.png) 24 25 #### Rendering audio graph 26 27 Audio graph rendering is done in blocks of sample-frames. The number of sample-frames in a block is called render quantum size, and the block itself is called a render quantum. 28 By default render quantum size value is 128 and it is constant. 29 30 The [`AudioContext`](/docs/core/audio-context) rendering thread is driven by a system-level audio callback. 31 Each call has a system-level audio callback buffer size, which is a varying number of sample-frames that needs to be computed on time before the next system-level audio callback arrives, 32 but render quantum size does not have to be a divisor of the system-level audio callback buffer size. 33 34 :::info 35 Concept of system-level audio callback does not apply to [`OfflineAudioContext`](/docs/core/offline-audio-context). 36 ::: 37 38 ## 7	# AudioScheduledSourceNode
8	
9	The `AudioScheduledSourceNode` interface is an [`AudioNode`](/docs/core/audio-node) which serves as a parent interface for several types of audio source nodes.
10	It provides ability to start and stop audio playback.
11	
12	Child classes:
13	 - [`AudioBufferBaseSourceNode`](/docs/sources/audio-buffer-base-source-node)
14	 - [`OscillatorNode`](/docs/sources/oscillator-node)
15	 - [`StreamerNode`](/docs/sources/streamer-node)

17	## Properties
18	
19	`AudioScheduledSourceNode` does not define any additional properties.
20	It inherits all properties from [`AudioNode`](/docs/core/audio-node#properties).
21	
22	## Methods
23	It inherits all methods from [`AudioNode`](/docs/core/audio-node#methods).
24	
25	### `start`
26	
27	Schedules the node to start audio playback at specified time. If no time is given, it starts immediately.
28	You can invoke this method only once in node's life.
29	
30	| Parameter | Type | Description |
31	| :---: | :---: | :---- |
32	| `when` | `number` | The time, in seconds, at which the node will start to play. |

35

38	| `RangeError` | `when` is negative number. |
39	| `InvalidStateError` | If node has already been started once. |
40	
41	#### Returns `undefined`.

44	
45	Schedules the node to stop audio playback at specified time. If no time is given, it stops immediately.
46	If you invoke this method multiple times on the same node before the designated stop time, the most recent call overwrites previous one.
47	
48	| Parameter | Type | Description |
49	| :---: | :---: | :---- |
50	| `when` | `number` | The time, in seconds, at which the node will stop playing. |

53	
54	| Error type | Description |
55	| :---: | :---- |
56	| `RangeError` | `when` is negative number. |
57	| `InvalidStateError` | If node has not been started yet. |

59	#### Returns `undefined`.

65	Sets (or remove) callback that will be fired when source node has stopped playing,
66	either because it's reached a predetermined stop time, the full duration of the audio has been performed, or because the entire buffer has been played.

22	| `playbackRate` | [`AudioParam`](/docs/core/audio-param) | [`k-rate`](/docs/core/audio-param#a-rate-vs-k-rate) `AudioParam` defining speed factor at which the audio will be played. |

25	
26	It inherits all methods from [`AudioScheduledSourceNode`](/docs/sources/audio-scheduled-source-node#methods).
27	
28	### `getLatency`
29	
30	Returns the playback latency introduced by the pitch correction algorithm, in seconds.
31	When scheduling precise playback times, start input samples this many seconds earlier to compensate for processing delay.
32	Typically around `0.06s` when pitch correction is enabled, and `0` otherwise.
33	
34	#### Returns `number`.
35	
36	<details>
37	<summary>Example usage</summary>
38	```tsx
39	const source = audioContext.createBufferSource({ pitchCorrection: true });
40	source.buffer = buffer;
41	source.connect(audioContext.destination);
42	
43	const latency = source.getLatency();
44	
45	// Schedule playback slightly earlier to compensate for latency
46	const startTime = audioContext.currentTime + 1.0; // play in 1 second
47	source.start(startTime - latency);
48	```
49	</details>

51	
52	## Events
53	
54	### `onPositionChanged` <MobileOnly />
55	
56	Allow to set (or remove) callback that will be fired after processing certain part of an audio.
57	Frequency is defined by `onPositionChangedInterval`. By setting this callback you can achieve pause functionality.
58	You can remove callback by passing `null`.
59	
60	### `onPositionChangedInterval` <MobileOnly />
61	
62	Allow to set frequency for `onPositionChanged` event. Value that can be set is around `1000/x` Hz.
63	
64	```ts
65	import { AudioContext, AudioBufferSourceNode } from 'react-native-audio-api';
66	
67	function App() {
68	    const ctx = new AudioContext();
69	    const sourceNode = ctx.createBufferSource();
70	    sourceNode.buffer = null; //set your buffer
71	    let offset = 0;
72	
73	    sourceNode.onPositionChanged = (event) => { //setting callback
74	        this.offset = event.value;
75	    };
76	
77	    sourceNode.onPositionChangedInterval = 100; //setting frequency to ~10Hz
78	
79	    sourceNode.start();
80	}
81	```

83	## Remarks
84	
85	#### `detune`
86	- Default value is 0.0.
87	- Nominal range is -∞ to ∞.
88	- For example value of 100 detune the source up by one semitone, whereas -1200 down by one octave.
89	- When `createBufferSource(true)` it is clamped to range -1200 to 1200.
90	
91	#### `playbackRate`
92	- Default value is 1.0.
93	- Nominal range is -∞ to ∞.
94	- For example value of 1.0 plays audio at normal speed, whereas value of 2.0 plays audio twice as fast as normal speed.
95	- When created with `createBufferSource(true)` it is clamped to range 0 to 3 and uses pitch correction algorithm.

content.text:
Here are the complete implementation details for `react-native-audio-api` (latest: **0.11.7**).

---

## 1. Loading and playing a local file URI

There are two approaches: the **standalone `decodeAudioData`** function (no AudioContext needed), or the **instance method `audioContext.decodeAudioData()`** (resamples to context's sampleRate automatically).

**Supported formats:** flac, mp3, ogg, opus, wav, aac, m4a, mp4.

**For a `file:///path/to/voice.ogg` URI:**

The `decodeAudioData` function (both standalone and on AudioContext) accepts a `string` input. The internal `AudioDecoder` class handles `file://` URIs by stripping the `file://` prefix before passing to the native decoder. So you can pass the full `file:///path/to/voice.ogg` string directly.

```ts
import { AudioContext, decodeAudioData } from 'react-native-audio-api';

// Option A: standalone (uses original sample rate)
const buffer = await decodeAudioData('file:///path/to/voice.ogg');

// Option B: via AudioContext (resamples to context's sampleRate)
const ctx = new AudioContext();
const buffer = await ctx.decodeAudioData('file:///path/to/voice.ogg');
```

The input type is `DecodeDataInput = number | string | ArrayBuffer`. Strings are classified as either remote (http/https) or local. Anything that is not `http://` or `https://` is treated as a local file path.

To play the decoded buffer:

```ts
const source = ctx.createBufferSource();
source.buffer = buffer;
source.connect(ctx.destination);
source.start(ctx.currentTime);
```

---

## 2. Playback progress (current time)

The `AudioBufferSourceNode` (via its parent `AudioBufferBaseSourceNode`) provides a **mobile-only** position callback system:

- **`onPositionChangedInterval`** -- `number` setter. Sets the callback frequency in milliseconds. E.g., `1000` = fires ~once per second; `100` = fires ~10 times per second.
- **`onPositionChanged`** -- setter accepting `((event: EventTypeWithValue) => void) | null`. The callback receives `{ value: number }` where **`value` is the elapsed playback position in seconds** (not milliseconds).

```ts
sourceNode.onPositionChangedInterval = 100; // ~10Hz updates
sourceNode.onPositionChanged = (event) => {
  const currentPositionSeconds = event.value;
};
```

The callback event type is `EventTypeWithValue` = `{ value: number }`.

To remove the callback: set `sourceNode.onPositionChanged = null`.

**Important:** the `value` is in **seconds**, not milliseconds. Multiply by 1000 if you need ms. You can compute progress percentage as `event.value / buffer.duration`.

Additionally, `AudioContext.currentTime` gives the context's ever-increasing hardware time in seconds (starts at 0, stops when suspended).

---

## 3. Pause, resume, and stop

**Critical design constraint:** An `AudioBufferSourceNode` can only be started once (calling `start()` twice throws `InvalidStateError`). The official example implements pause/resume by:

1. **Pause:** call `sourceNode.stop(ctx.currentTime)` then `await ctx.suspend()`. Track `currentElapsedTime` from the last `onPositionChanged` callback.
2. **Resume:** call `await ctx.resume()`, create a **new** `AudioBufferSourceNode`, set its `buffer` to the same `AudioBuffer`, connect it, and call `sourceNode.start(ctx.currentTime, currentElapsedTime)` -- the second argument is the **offset** (in seconds) into the buffer to resume from.
3. **Stop:** call `sourceNode.stop(ctx.currentTime)`.

The `start()` method signature:
```ts
start(when?: number, offset?: number, duration?: number): void
```
- `when` -- scheduled start time in AudioContext seconds (0 = immediately)
- `offset` -- position in the buffer to begin playback (seconds)
- `duration` -- how long to play (optional; omit to play to end)

The `stop()` method signature:
```ts
stop(when?: number): void
```
- `when` -- scheduled stop time (0 = immediately)

`AudioContext` methods:
- `suspend(): Promise<boolean>` -- pauses time progression
- `resume(): Promise<boolean>` -- resumes from suspended state
- `close(): Promise<undefined>` -- releases audio resources
- `state` property: `'running' | 'suspended' | 'closed'`

---

## 4. Playback completion callback (onEnded)

Defined on `AudioScheduledSourceNode` (parent of `AudioBufferSourceNode`):

```ts
sourceNode.onEnded = () => {
  console.log('Playback finished');
};
```

Fires when the source node stops playing -- either from reaching the end of the buffer, a scheduled stop time, or an explicit `stop()` call.

The setter accepts `((event: EventEmptyType) => void) | null`. `EventEmptyType` is `{}` (empty object).

Returns an `AudioEventSubscription` which has a `.remove()` method:
```ts
const subscription = sourceNode.onEnded = () => { ... };
subscription.remove(); // unsubscribe
```

Or set to `null` to remove: `sourceNode.onEnded = null`.

---

## 5. Exact import paths and class/function names

Everything is exported from the top-level `'react-native-audio-api'`:

```ts
import {
  // Core
  AudioContext,          // class -- new AudioContext({ sampleRate?: number })
  AudioBuffer,           // class (type)
  AudioBufferSourceNode, // class (type) -- created via ctx.createBufferSource()
  AudioParam,            // class (type)
  GainNode,              // class (type) -- created via ctx.createGain()
  AudioDestinationNode,  // class (type)
  AudioNode,             // class (type, base)
  BaseAudioContext,       // class (type, base)
  OfflineAudioContext,   // class

  // Standalone decoder (no AudioContext needed)
  decodeAudioData,       // async function(input: string | number | ArrayBuffer, sampleRate?: number, fetchOptions?: RequestInit): Promise<AudioBuffer>
  decodePCMInBase64,     // async function(base64: string, sampleRate: number, channelCount: number, isInterleaved?: boolean): Promise<AudioBuffer>

  // System
  AudioManager,          // singleton -- setAudioSessionOptions, setAudioSessionActivity, etc.

  // Notifications
  PlaybackNotificationManager, // singleton
  RecordingNotificationManager, // singleton
} from 'react-native-audio-api';
```

**Key types** (also exported from same path):
```ts
import type {
  AudioContextOptions,      // { sampleRate?: number }
  AudioBufferSourceOptions, // { buffer?, loop?, loopStart?, loopEnd?, pitchCorrection?, playbackRate?, detune? }
  ContextState,             // 'running' | 'suspended' | 'closed'
  DecodeDataInput,          // number | string | ArrayBuffer
} from 'react-native-audio-api';
```

**Event types** (exported from same path):
```ts
import type {
  EventEmptyType,      // {} -- used by onEnded
  EventTypeWithValue,  // { value: number } -- used by onPositionChanged
} from 'react-native-audio-api';
```

---

## Summary of the pause/resume pattern (from official AudioPlayer example)

The official example at `apps/common-app/src/examples/AudioFile/AudioPlayer.ts` demonstrates the canonical pattern:

- One long-lived `AudioContext` instance
- One cached `AudioBuffer` (decoded once, reused)
- A **new** `AudioBufferSourceNode` is created on every `play()` call
- `currentElapsedTime` is tracked via `onPositionChanged` callbacks
- Pause = `stop()` + `suspend()`; Resume = `resume()` + create new source node + `start(time, offset)`
- The `buffer` property on `AudioBufferSourceNode` can only be set **once** per node instance (throws `InvalidStateError` on second set)
